subject: electronics
title: Sensor divider: darkness switches the lamp on

questions.prompt: Which statement about the sensor divider is correct?

choices.text: As it gets darker the voltage across the LDR falls, so the lamp switches off
The output voltage stays at 3.0 V whatever the light level
As the LDR resistance rises in the dark, its share of the 6 V supply rises until it crosses the 4.5 V threshold and switches the lamp on.
The fixed resistor always takes the bigger share of the supply

questions.misconception: As it gets darker and the LDR's resistance rises, the voltage across the LDR falls, so the sensor output switches the lamp off.
questions.explanation: The trap claim is: As it gets darker and the LDR's resistance rises, the voltage across the LDR falls, so the sensor output switches the lamp off. In fact In a series divider each resistor takes a share of the supply in proportion to its resistance, so as the LDR's resistance rises in the dark its share - the output voltage - climbs until it crosses the threshold and switches the lamp on.

questions.prompt: Why does the output reach exactly 3.0 V when the light first falls?

choices.text: Because the threshold is set at 3.0 V
Because the LDR resistance steps up to 1 kOhm, equal to the fixed resistor, so equal resistances split the 6 V supply evenly
Because the supply voltage drops to 3.0 V
Because the lamp draws half the current

questions.explanation: Scene 2 works this: equal resistances of 1 kOhm each split the supply evenly, so the output across the LDR climbs to 3.0 V.

questions.prompt: A student says the voltage across the LDR falls as it gets darker. Explain, in two sentences, what actually happens to the output as light falls.
questions.answer: In a series divider each resistor takes a share of the supply in proportion to its resistance, so as the LDR's resistance rises in the dark its share - the output voltage - climbs until it crosses the threshold and switches the lamp on.
questions.explanation: The share rule is the deciding habit: name the rising resistance first, then the rising share that crosses the threshold.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, state the output voltage at dusk and whether the lamp is on, and why.
questions.answer: At dusk the output is 4.2 V and the lamp stays off, because 4.2 V is still just below the 4.5 V threshold.
questions.explanation: Scene 3 shows dusk: the output climbs to 4.2 V, close to but still below the 4.5 V threshold.

questions.prompt: Which list gives the divided voltages across the LDR, in scene order?

choices.text: 1.2 V in bright daylight, 3.0 V as light falls, 4.2 V at dusk, 5.4 V in the dark
5.4 V in bright daylight, 4.2 V as light falls, 3.0 V at dusk, 1.2 V in the dark
3.0 V in bright daylight, 1.2 V as light falls, 5.4 V at dusk, 4.2 V in the dark
4.2 V in bright daylight, 5.4 V as light falls, 1.2 V at dusk, 3.0 V in the dark

questions.explanation: Scene 1 gives 1.2 V, scene 2 gives 3.0 V, scene 3 gives 4.2 V, and scene 4 gives 5.4 V as the LDR resistance climbs.
